a
6y−2x2y−2y3

decision.explanation: For the upper surface z=4-x²-y², the outward vector area element is ⟨2x,2y,1⟩ dA, so its flux integrand is 2y(4-x²-y²)-y. The bottom disk has outward normal ⟨0,0,-1⟩ and contributes y. Adding gives 8y-2x²y-2y³, option e. All displayed expressions integrate to zero over the symmetric disk D, but e directly represents the combined surface contributions.

Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,z,\,-y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
after.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,R=-y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-0\cdot (-2x)-(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)+(-y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,z,-y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨0,z,−y⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
6y−2x2y−2y3
b
4y−2x2y−2y3
c
2x2y+2y3−8y
d
2x2y+2y3−6y
e
8y−2x2y−2y3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=4−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper paraboloid S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(4−x2−y2)=−2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(4−x2−y2)=−2y

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=0,Q=z=4−x2−y2,R=−y.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D(−0⋅(−2x)−(4−x2−y2)⋅(−2y)+(−y))dA=∬D(7y−2x2y−2y3)dA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨0,z,−y⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬DydA.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D(7y−2x2y−2y3)dA+∬DydA=∬D8y−2x2y−2y3dA.

Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,z,\,-y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
content.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,R=-y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-0\cdot (-2x)-(4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)+(-y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,z,-y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(7y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}8y-2{x}^{2}y-2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F=⟨y,0,2x⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of the solid onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
4x−xyx2+y2
b
xyx2+y2−4x
c
−xyx2+y2
d
xyx2+y2
e
xyx2+y2−2x

decision.explanation: The lower cone z=√(x²+y²)-2 has outward vector area element ⟨x/√(x²+y²),y/√(x²+y²),-1⟩ dA. Its flux integrand is xy/√(x²+y²)-2x. The upper disk has outward normal ⟨0,0,1⟩ and contributes 2x. Their sum is xy/√(x²+y²), giving d. All displayed integrands integrate to zero over the symmetric disk, but d directly combines the two surface contributions. The undefined value at the origin does not affect the integral.

Consider the vector field $F=⟨y,\,0,\,2x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of the solid onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
after.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=0$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper plane ${S}_{1}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is upward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨y,0,2x⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower cone ${S}_{2}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2)=\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=2x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂h}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-y\cdot \frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-0\cdot \frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-2x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

Consider the vector field F=⟨y,0,2x⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of the solid onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
4x−xyx2+y2
b
xyx2+y2−4x
c
−xyx2+y2
d
xyx2+y2
e
xyx2+y2−2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=0 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=x2+y2−2 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper plane S1.

    Since the positive orientation is upward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬S1F⋅ndS=∬D⟨y,0,2x⟩⋅⟨0,0,1⟩dA=∬D2xdA.

  • Consider the lower cone S2.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=h(x,y): ∂h∂x=∂∂x(x2+y2−2)=xx2+y2∂h∂y=∂∂y(x2+y2−2)=yx2+y2

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=y,Q=0,R=2x.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=−∬D(−P∂h∂x−Q∂h∂y+R)dA=−∬D(−y⋅xx2+y2−0⋅yx2+y2+2x)dA=∬D(xyx2+y2−2x)dA.

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D2xdA+∬D(xyx2+y2−2x)dA=∬Dxyx2+y2dA.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms d: the upward-oriented top contributes 2x, and the downward-oriented cone contributes xy/√(x²+y²)-2x. Adding cancels the 2x terms. Option e describes only the cone's contribution. Although all choices integrate to zero over the symmetric disk, d is the direct combined integrand.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081085/assets/e61f3d7c23ef7876bec2f11c93974551058bcd32f28745898604926d84dbcfee.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨y,\,0,\,2x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of the solid onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
content.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=0$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper plane ${S}_{1}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is upward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨y,0,2x⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower cone ${S}_{2}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-2)=\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=2x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂h}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-y\cdot \frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-0\cdot \frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-2x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{xy}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: For the upper hemisphere g=√(1-x²-y²), the outward vector area element is ⟨-g_x,-g_y,1⟩ dA. Dotting with F=⟨1,x,0⟩ gives (x+xy)/√(1-x²-y²). ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081085/assets/8a48be0b4c101babf157a05959e923576ad5614113b3eec9e93fe747d5dc3803.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨1,\,x,\,0⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
after.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper hemisphere ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=1,\,Q=x,\,R=0.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-1\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})-x\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})+0\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨1,x,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}0\,\text{d}A \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A+0 \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨1,x,0⟩ and the closed surface S that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
y−x1−x2−y2
b
x+y1−x2−y2
c
xy−y1−x2−y2
d
x+xy1−x2−y2
e
xy1−x2−y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=1−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper hemisphere S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(1−x2−y2)=−x1−x2−y2∂g∂y=∂∂y(1−x2−y2)=−y1−x2−y2

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=1,Q=x,R=0.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D−1⋅(−x1−x2−y2)−x⋅(−y1−x2−y2)+0dA=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA.

  • Consider the lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨1,x,0⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D0dA=0.

Therefore, the flux of F across the entire surface is ∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA+0=∬Dx+xy1−x2−y2dA.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081085/assets/8a48be0b4c101babf157a05959e923576ad5614113b3eec9e93fe747d5dc3803.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨1,\,x,\,0⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that represents the boundary of the solid shown above. Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
content.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So, 

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper hemisphere ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=1,\,Q=x,\,R=0.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-1\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})-x\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}})+0\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨1,x,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}0\,\text{d}A \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $F$ across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A+0 \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{x+xy}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨0,−z,2y⟩ and the closed surface S that encloses the finite region between the cone z=4−x2+y2 and the plane z=0. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
 y−2yx2+y2
b
 −4yx2+y2
c
 2y+4yx2+y2
d
 4y+2yx2+y2
e
y−4yx2+y2
Submit

decision.explanation: Write r=√(x²+y²). The upper cone has outward vector area element ⟨x/r,y/r,1⟩ dA, giving flux integrand −(4−r)y/r+2y=3y−4y/r. The downward-oriented bottom contributes −2y. Adding gives y−4y/r, option e. All choices integrate to zero over the symmetric disk D, but e directly combines the surface contributions.

after.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,-z,\,2y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the cone $z=4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and the plane $z=0.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
after.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper cone ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=-z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4,\,R=2y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(0)\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})-(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4)\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,-z,2y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2y)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Consider the vector field F=⟨0,−z,2y⟩ and the closed surface S that encloses the finite region between the cone z=4−x2+y2 and the plane z=0. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
 y−2yx2+y2
b
 −4yx2+y2
c
 2y+4yx2+y2
d
 4y+2yx2+y2
e
y−4yx2+y2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=4−x2+y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=0 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper cone S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(4−x2+y2)=−xx2+y2∂g∂y=∂∂y(4−x2+y2)=−yx2+y2

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=0,Q=−z=x2+y2−4,R=2y.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D(−(0)⋅(−xx2+y2)−(x2+y2−4)⋅(−yx2+y2)+2y)dA=∬D(y−4yx2+y2+2y)dA=∬D(3y−4yx2+y2)dA.

  • Consider lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨0,−z,2y⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D(−2y)dA.

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D(3y−4yx2+y2)dA+∬D(−2y)dA=∬Dy−4yx2+y2dA.

All displayed expressions integrate to zero over the symmetric disk, but e directly represents the combined surface contributions.

content.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,-z,\,2y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the cone $z=4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and the plane $z=0.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
content.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=0$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper cone ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=-z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4,\,R=2y.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(0)\cdot (-\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})-(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-4)\cdot (-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨0,-z,2y⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2y)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y-\frac{4y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨y,\,0,\,-z⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the paraboloids $z=1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ and $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
after.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=-z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (-2x)-(0)\cdot (-2y)+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower paraboloid ${S}_{2}.$ 

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)=2x \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)=2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=-z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂h}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (2x)-(0)\cdot (2y)+4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-2xy+4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4xy+2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-5\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

content.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=-z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (-2x)-(0)\cdot (-2y)+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the lower paraboloid ${S}_{2}.$ 

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)=2x \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)=2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=y,\,Q=0,\,R=-z=4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is downward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂h}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (2x)-(0)\cdot (2y)+4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-2xy+4-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(2xy+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4xy+2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-5\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
